build_plan.exit_criteria: The exact gargoyle STL is nonempty, manifold, watertight, one connected shell, standard-nozzle thickness checked, and visually proves both the seated and tail-caught endpoints.

components.duty: The rigid gargoyle carries every visible character feature, rocks as one body on its belly, and arrests its 70 degree nose-down travel on the broad inner face of its own tail.
components.form: One fused 113 x 84 x 62 mm printable solid with a horned head, four paws, swept wings, convex belly, and a curled tail defining one open rear throat.
components.interfaces: One convex belly fulcrum bears on the edge while one broad integral tail pad provides the terminal catch; there are zero pins, axles, fasteners, or loose pieces.
components.name: One-piece Gutterfall gargoyle
components.placement: The 30 mm open belly-tail throat seats over one 18–28 mm furniture edge with the head and forepaws facing open air and the tail remaining behind the edge.

concept.interaction: Seat the gargoyle's open belly-tail throat over an 18–28 mm table edge, press its shoulders toward open air, release the single rigid gargoyle to roll nose-down 70 degrees until its own tail pad catches, then lift the gargoyle back around the edge to reset.
concept.summary: A single chunky one-piece gargoyle uses its convex belly as a table-lip rocker and the broad inner pad of its curled tail as its visible arresting catch.
concept.title: Gutterfall

research.basis: Wish-authored dimensional and behavioral specification; no external component or standard-part geometry is used.
research.physical_evidence_limit: Digital geometry can establish shape, clearances, topology, manifoldness, thickness, and modeled state relationships, but not real-world friction, impact response, furniture finish compatibility, or successful physical catching.
